correctness.rationale: The ordered 7-by-49 Gabor matrix and the ±1 domain are explicit. Shift/reversal/sign operations permute all 49 columns, up to one invertible row permutation; nine class orbits partition all 64 normalized windows. For each representative, all seven integer coefficients of its selected 7-by-7 determinant (5040 permutation terms) vanish exactly. The embedded check_exact.py reconstructs all group orbits and each determinant from scratch, and check_modular.py independently checks six finite-field specializations. Complex vanishing follows from the integer identities, not the modular results. Thus every one of 128 sign windows has a singular 7-column selection; nothing is asserted about spark size below seven.

Neither similarity search nor finite partition proves historical novelty; unindexed calculations and a 2026 complex-perturbation source not read in full remain bounded risks.

value.rationale: Full spark is the canonical worst-case erasure property: any seven Gabor measurements reconstruct a seven-coordinate signal precisely when every maximal minor is nonzero. Discrete sign alphabets are naturally constrained hardware phase designs. The theorem supplies a global obstruction for every sign window at the first investigated seven-cycle beyond the five-cycle sign existence case, plus nine reusable exact integer obstruction certificates. This is a meaningful strict design limitation, not a genericity exercise or an unsupported numerical guess.
